advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Defer the _latest_review_result_timestamp filesystem read until the terminal branch where latest_reviewed_at is actually meaningful.
evidence: gate_runs.py:206: `latest = _latest_review_result_timestamp(ticket_id, repo_root)` runs before the terminal-status branch
gate_runs.py:214-216: `if status not in _TERMINAL_STATUSES: out["reason"] = f"run-{status}"; return out` — the diagnostic latest is included but readability is already decided
advisory.finding: _review_result_status calls _latest_review_result_timestamp (which does a resolver lookup + os.listdir on the ticket dir) unconditionally before the status check, so it runs on every poll — including frequent 'running'/non-terminal polls where the latest_reviewed_at value is only a diagnostic and readability is fixed to False.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert the emitted `sidecar_reviewed_at` equals the REVIEW_RESULT filename prefix (or drive a real emit through gate_run_status and assert findings.readable is True).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/gate_runs.py:176 `prefix = f"{reviewed_at}-"` — readability hinges on sidecar_reviewed_at matching the on-disk filename prefix

No test drives sidecar.emit and then asserts _has_review_result_timestamp / gate_run_status returns readable=True using the REAL emitted filename (all gate_status tests use fabricated _write_review_result files with a fabricated prefix)
advisory.finding: test_latest_review_result_returns_newest_payload_with_prose asserts only `isinstance(first['sidecar_reviewed_at'], int)` — it never asserts the returned timestamp EQUALS the emitted event's filename-prefix timestamp. That equality is exactly the invariant _has_review_result_timestamp relies on (it matches files by `f"{reviewed_at}-"` prefix), so the round-trip is unverified.
scenarios: If append_event's returned timestamp ever diverged in units/format from the sidecar filename prefix (e.g. seconds vs ns), _has_review_result_timestamp would never match and every run would report readable=False, but the isinstance-only assertion would still pass

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a reuse test that populates multiple retained REVIEW_RESULT sidecars and asserts _latest_reusable_review returns the newest via the all_review_results branch.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:54-57 `reviews = sidecar.all_review_results(...)` then `return reviews[0]` before falling back to latest_review_result

tests/unit/test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py:127 monkeypatches `reuse.sidecar.latest_review_result` only; search for `all_review_results` in test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py and test_plan_review_reuse.py returns (no matches)

Named untested input: a ticket with multiple retained REVIEW_RESULT sidecars where all_review_results[0] and latest_review_result would differ — the branch selecting all_review_results[0] is unverified
advisory.finding: `_latest_reusable_review` adds a new primary branch that prefers `all_review_results(...)[0]` and only falls back to `latest_review_result`; the existing reuse tests monkeypatch only `latest_review_result` (the fallback), so the new all_review_results-first branch is never exercised.
scenarios: A regression making all_review_results return an out-of-order list (older-first) would pick the wrong prior review for reuse, undetected by tests that only stub the fallback

blocking.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting a reused PASS and reused BLOCK verdict carry `sidecar_reviewed_at` from the prior sidecar and that gate_status.findings.readable resolves correctly for a reused run.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:192 `"sidecar_reviewed_at": prior.get("reviewed_at"),` (added to reused PASS verdict) and reuse.py:269 (added to reused BLOCK verdict)

search for `sidecar_reviewed_at` in tests returns only test_gate_status_sidecar_visibility.py (fabricated records) and test_sidecar_reader.py (fresh emit) — no hit in test_plan_review_reuse.py or test_plan_review_reuse_replay.py

test_gate_status_sidecar_visibility.py:test_gate_status_treats_reused_sidecar_receipt_as_readable feeds a hand-built record with sidecar_emitted=False; it never exercises reuse.py producing sidecar_reviewed_at from prior.get('reviewed_at')
Named untested input: idempotent_reuse / verdict_reuse on a ticket whose prior sidecar has reviewed_at=<ns> must yield verdict['sidecar_reviewed_at']==<ns>; unasserted.
blocking.finding: reuse.py now stamps `sidecar_reviewed_at` on both the reused-PASS and reused-BLOCK verdicts (the field that lets gate_status compute findings.readable for a REUSED plan review), but no test asserts a reused verdict carries `sidecar_reviewed_at`, and none drives a reused-review daemon run to confirm the receipt reaches gate_status.findings. The reuse-replay/reuse suites were not updated for this new field.
scenarios: A reused plan-review PASS/BLOCK whose prior sidecar lacks a `reviewed_at` key would stamp None, silently degrading findings.readable to 'review-result-generation-unknown' with no test to catch it

dropped.finding: _latest_reusable_review's fallback to sidecar.latest_review_result is unreachable dead code: all_review_results and latest_review_result walk the same ticket dir with identical filename filter and schema guard, so all_review_results is non-empty whenever any usable review exists. Additionally, only all_review_results stamps 'reviewed_at' onto the payload (sidecar.py:249) while latest_review_result does not, so were the fallback ever reached prior.get('reviewed_at') would be None and the reuse-path sidecar_reviewed_at receipt would silently be lost.
